hypothesis.statement: At least one tested coordinate factor-base family retains at least 0.8 times both matched-null five-term supports, reaches full relation rank and verified individual descent, reduces the advice-bit online-query-squared diagnostic by at least 20 percent against both random-x and random-scalar, and beats fixed-base BSGS at the same advice-bit budget on clean toy fixed curves.
hypothesis.mechanism: Precompute every four-term point sum with a bounded list of source witnesses. For a target Q, scan F and query whether Q-P lies in the compiled four-sum table. Known multiples aG yield linear equations in the unknown factor-base logarithms; a full-rank system recovers those logarithms, after which randomized five-term descent recovers an arbitrary toy target logarithm.
assumptions: UNTESTED: coordinate-defined factor bases may have a better support-versus-witness-advice tradeoff than matched random-x sets.
HEURISTIC: behavior at 12-16 bits can route larger experiments but cannot establish an asymptotic exponent.

MODEL-BOUND: S*T^2/(epsilon*q) is compared to the generic fixed-generator preprocessing theorem only as a unit-disclosed diagnostic; the concrete coordinate compiler is non-generic and the theorem hides logarithmic factors.
HEURISTIC: serialized bytes and logical lookup traffic are portable accounting proxies, not measured memory-controller traffic.
TOY-EVIDENCE: exhaustive group support and independent scalar verification are feasible only because the scheduled groups are tiny.

predictions.metric: exact five-term support ratio to each matched null family
predictions.minimum_effect: at least 0.80 on every promoted instance

predictions.metric: relation matrix rank and factor-base logarithm verification
predictions.minimum_effect: rank equals factor-base size and every recovered logarithm reproduces its point
every scheduled challenge is recovered and verified within the frozen attempt budget

predictions.metric: advice-bit online-query-squared diagnostic ratio to each matched null family
predictions.minimum_effect: at most 0.80 while the support-retention gate holds

predictions.metric: online group operations versus fixed-base BSGS at the same advice-bit budget
predictions.minimum_effect: both sampled average and deterministic worst-case bound are lower

falsification_conditions: No coordinate family simultaneously passes exact support retention, full relation rank, verified factor-base logarithms, and individual descent on the scheduled clean curves.

Any apparent diagnostic improvement disappears when factor-base construction, full four-sum enumeration, witness payloads, target generation, unsuccessful queries, rank work, or descent randomization is charged.
The scalar-progression control is the only family that compresses advice, indicating that the signal depends on disclosed scalar structure.
Independent reconstruction disagrees with any curve, factor base, support, witness, relation equation, rank, solution, descent, operation count, or source hash.
A stronger matched rho or fixed-curve generic preprocessing baseline dominates the claimed end-to-end cost.
interpretation_limits: A passing functional gate would be the first end-to-end toy relation workflow in this harness, not evidence of a sub-rho exponent.
A 20 percent toy diagnostic win is a routing signal, not a proof that the generic preprocessing frontier is beaten asymptotically.
The compiler materializes four-sum support and therefore is expected to have large offline and storage costs.
Sparse linear algebra at cryptographic factor-base sizes, large-prime variants, and a fitted total exponent below 0.5 remain later gates.
No real key, wallet, standardized-curve challenge, or unauthorized target is in scope.

instances: three deterministic clean prime-order curves per bit size over distinct seeded field primes
